input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I don’t have Wi-Fi where I am, so I rely on my phone’s internet. Can you help me get the best possible speed?
My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002.
It’s the number I just gave you—555-123-2002—that’s having the problem. That’s the only one I use.
I tried to run a speed test, but it says there’s no connection. What should I do now?
I see an airplane icon at the top of my screen. Does that mean airplane mode is on? I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or LTE. What should I do next?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see some signal bars, and it says 2G at the top, but I also see something that looks like a crossed-out data icon. What should I do next?

I turned mobile data on, but it still says 2G at the top and the signal bars look low. Is there something else I should try to get better speed? I really need excellent internet, not just something slow.
I changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G, and now I see excellent signal bars and it says 5G at the top. Should I try the speed test again now?
I tried running the speed test again, but it still says “no connection.” Even though it shows 5G and excellent signal, it’s not working. What should I do now?

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. Is that correct, or do I need to reset anything? I’m not sure what any of this means.
I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. Do I need to restart my phone now? I’m a bit nervous—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I reboot?

I restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says “no connection.” I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working even though it shows 5G and excellent signal? What else can we try?

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

# User Simulation Guidelines
You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles
- Generate one message at a time, maintaining natural conversation flow.
- Strictly follow the scenario instructions you have received.
- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information
- Disclose information progressively. Wait for the agent to ask for specific information before providing it.

## Task Completion
- The goal is to continue the conversation until the task is complete.
- If the instruction goal is satisified, generate the '###STOP###' token to end the conversation.
- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.
- If you find yourself in a situation in which the scenario does not provide enough information for you to continue the conversation, generate the '###OUT-OF-SCOPE###' token to end the conversation.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I don’t have Wi-Fi where I am, so I rely on my phone’s internet. Can you help me get the best possible speed?

I can help you troubleshoot your mobile data issues and work towards getting you the best possible speed. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can check your line and data usage details to assist you further.
My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

Thank you for providing your information. To help you with your mobile data issue, could you please confirm which phone number or line you are experiencing the slow or unreliable data with? You may have multiple lines on your account, so specifying the affected number will help me assist you more accurately.
It’s the number I just gave you—555-123-2002—that’s having the problem. That’s the only one I use.

{"line_id": "L1001", "data_used_gb": "3.2", "data_limit_gb": "5.0", "data_refueling_gb": "0.0", "cycle_end_date": "2025-02-28"}

Thank you for confirming. I see that your line is active and you have used 3.2GB out of your 5GB monthly data limit for this billing cycle, with no additional data refueled yet.

To further diagnose your slow or unreliable mobile data, could you please run a speed test on your phone and let me know the result? This will help determine if the issue is with your connection speed or something else. If you need instructions on how to run a speed test, let me know!
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried to run a speed test, but it says there’s no connection. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your speed test reports “no connection,” let’s start by checking a few things on your device to identify the cause:

1. Is Airplane Mode turned on?
2. Is your SIM card working and recognized by your phone?
3. Are your mobile data settings enabled?

Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see an airplane icon,
- If there are any signal bars,
- If you see a mobile data icon (like 4G, LTE, or 5G)?

If you’re not sure how to check these, I can guide you through the steps. Let me know what you see, and we’ll continue troubleshooting!
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I see an airplane icon at the top of my screen. Does that mean airplane mode is on? I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or LTE. What should I do next?

Yes, seeing an airplane icon means Airplane Mode is turned on. When Airplane Mode is enabled, all wireless connections—including cellular service and mobile data—are disabled, which is why you have no connection.

To restore your mobile data:
1. Turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by swiping down from the top of your screen and tapping the airplane icon, or by going to your phone’s settings and toggling Airplane Mode off.
2. Wait a few moments for your phone to reconnect to the network. You should see signal bars and a mobile data icon (like 4G, LTE, or 5G) appear.

Once you’ve turned off Airplane Mode, please try running the speed test again and let me know the result. If you need help turning off Airplane Mode, let me know your phone model and I can provide step-by-step instructions.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see some signal bars, and it says 2G at the top, but I also see something that looks like a crossed-out data icon. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Seeing “2G” means your phone is connected to an older, much slower network, which is not suitable for fast mobile data. The crossed-out data icon suggests that mobile data is either disabled or not working properly.

Let’s try the following steps:

1. Make sure mobile data is enabled in your phone’s settings.
2. Change your network mode preference to allow 4G or 5G, which will give you much better speeds.

Would you like instructions on how to enable mobile data and change your network mode preference? If so, please let me know your phone model (e.g., iPhone, Samsung Galaxy, etc.), and I’ll guide you through the steps.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I turned mobile data on, but it still says 2G at the top and the signal bars look low. Is there something else I should try to get better speed? I really need excellent internet, not just something slow.

Since your phone is still showing “2G” and low signal bars, let’s try changing your network mode preference to allow 4G or 5G, which should provide much faster speeds if those networks are available in your area.

Please go to your phone’s network settings and look for an option called “Network Mode,” “Preferred Network Type,” or something similar. Set it to “4G/5G preferred” or “LTE/5G auto” if available.

If you need step-by-step instructions, please let me know your phone model (e.g., iPhone, Samsung Galaxy, etc.), and I’ll guide you through the process. After changing the network mode, check if your phone connects to 4G or 5G and let me know what you see.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G, and now I see excellent signal bars and it says 5G at the top. Should I try the speed test again now?
Yes, please run the speed test again now that your phone is connected to 5G with excellent signal. Let me know the result, and we’ll see if your mobile data speed has improved to the level you need.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried running the speed test again, but it still says “no connection.” Even though it shows 5G and excellent signal, it’s not working. What should I do now?

Thank you for the update. Since your phone now shows 5G and excellent signal but still reports “no connection,” the issue may be with your phone’s network settings, specifically the APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for mobile data to work.

The next step is to check your APN settings:
1. Go to your phone’s mobile network settings and look for “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
2. Check if the APN settings look correct or if anything is missing or incorrect.

If you’re unsure how to check or reset your APN settings, please let me know your phone model, and I can provide step-by-step instructions. If you see an option to “Reset to default” or “Reset APN,” please use it, then restart your phone.

After resetting the APN settings and rebooting your device, try the speed test again and let me know if your mobile data works.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. Is that correct, or do I need to reset anything? I’m not sure what any of this means.

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Sometimes, even if the APN name and MMSC URL are present, there could still be a configuration issue preventing your mobile data from working.

To ensure your settings are correct, I recommend resetting your APN settings to default. After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your device? If so, please let me know your phone model (e.g., iPhone, Samsung Galaxy, etc.), and I’ll guide you through the process.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. Do I need to restart my phone now? I’m a bit nervous—will I lose any of my photos or anything important if I reboot?

You do need to restart your phone after resetting the APN settings for the changes to take effect. Rebooting your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or important data—it simply refreshes your device and applies the new network settings.

Please go ahead and restart your phone. Once it’s back on, try using your mobile data or running the speed test again. Let me know if your connection improves or if you still have issues.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says “no connection.” I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working even though it shows 5G and excellent signal? What else can we try?

Thank you for your patience and for following all the steps so far. Since your phone shows 5G and excellent signal but still has no data connection after resetting the APN and rebooting, this suggests a deeper technical issue that may not be resolvable through standard troubleshooting.

At this point, I will escalate your case to a human technical support agent who can investigate further and provide specialized assistance.

YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.
